chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:

Feed your pregnant women the dairy (products), so if there happens to be a boy in her belly, he would come out as pure of heart, knowledgeable, brave; and if there happens to be a girl, she would be of beautiful in her appearance, and in her manners, and of large buttocks, and she would enjoy with her husband.

key_terms.حَبَالَاكُمْ: Your pregnant women (literally: your carrying ones)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended dietary practices for pregnant women in Shia tradition to benefit the child's character and health?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Imam al-Rida (AS), this hadith highlights the Shia belief in the physical and spiritual impact of maternal nutrition on fetal development. It specifically recommends feeding 'luban' (likely frankincense or a specific dairy product) to pregnant women, promising that a son will be pure-hearted, knowledgeable, and courageous, while a daughter will possess beauty, good character, and marital favor. This reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on nurturing the next generation through both physical care and spiritual well-being.
